Washed, or just slumping?

Not washed as a runner, but the 2024 Barkley isn't coming back, and the numbers say don't pay for a rebound.

2024 was the outlier. About half of his edge that year was the best run game in football: the Eagles' line and scheme ranked 1st of 32 in the credit model. They ranked 12th in 2025 and 29th so far in 2026. His own rush yards over expected went from 2nd in the league (+1.6 per carry) to 31st of 49 (+0.2). Rushing efficiency barely repeats from year to year, so his true level sits between those seasons. Our best estimate puts him at about a league-average runner.

He can still run. In 2026 he has 5.1 yards per carry and +1.1 over expected (6th), but on 36 carries, which is too few to mean much either way. In his two full games he had 88% of the team's designed runs, a full workload worth 12.6 expected points a game. He scored 9.0 with no touchdowns, and Jalen Hurts takes 40% of the Eagles' runs inside the 5.

The red flags are age and health. He had two partial games, then sat out Week 5 with a hamstring injury. History is not kind to that start. Backs whose early slump included a partial game got back to 90% of the year before only about 1 time in 10. And at 29, only about 1 in 5 top-24 backs stay top 24 the next year. The injury type is one of the milder ones, though. Backs coming back from a hamstring scored a median 72% of their pre-injury points per game the rest of the way, against 84% for uninjured backs over the same weeks, and none of the 14 missed time again with it that season. Barkley has never had a hamstring injury before. After his three ankle sprains he came back at 97%, 66% and 88% of his previous level.

The trade, by these numbers. When he plays, Barkley projects at about 9–10 PPR points a game for the rest of 2026 and in 2027. Cook projects at 16.0 and 14.5. You would be swapping your most reliable back, who is 26, for an aging back in a declining run game plus McConkey, who is also slumping. Woody Marks adds little either way: he was 99th of 100 in points over expected in 2025. On these numbers, the deal only makes sense if you believe in a McConkey breakout. Every estimate here has wide ranges, and the model cannot see the hamstring prognosis.

The trade on the table

You give James Cook (maybe with Woody Marks) for Saquon Barkley and Ladd McConkey. Keeper league, so both the rest of 2026 and 2027 count. Projections come from a model tested season by season against simply carrying forward last year's or this year's points per game; 80% ranges show how wide the honest answer is.

Which numbers are skill?

Year-to-year carry-over

Correlation of each number with the same back's number the next season (backs with 150+ carries or 40+ targets in both, 2016–2025, season effects removed), with 80% intervals. 1 = perfectly repeatable, 0 = pure noise. Survivors only, so read each as roughly ±0.1.

The best backs, side by side

All sixteen for the selected view. Expected points = what his carries and targets are worth for an average back given down, distance, field position and pass depth; points over expected is the rest (efficiency plus touchdown luck). Select a row to put that back in the comparison.

The back, or the line?

A ridge regression on every designed run since 2016 credits each carry's EPA to the runner, his team that season (line and scheme), the play-caller and the defense, after adjusting for down, distance, field position, score, quarter and box count. Each season's EPA per carry above league average splits into those parts and sums exactly. "Back" = his career estimate plus whatever that season beat the model by (form and luck).

Season by season

How this was built

Data
nflverse play-by-play and weekly stats (2006–2026), participation (who was on the field, 2016–2025), Next Gen Stats rushing (yards over expected, box counts, 2016+), Pro Football Reference contact stats (yards before and after contact, broken tackles, 2018+), FTN charting (2022+). Regular season only. Points are nflverse PPR, which matches your league: 1 per catch, 0.1 per yard, 6 per TD, −2 per fumble lost.
Designed runs
Shares and efficiency use designed runs: QB scrambles and kneels are left out. Goal-line QB share = the team's designed runs inside the 5 taken by the QB (Hurts and Allen are the extremes).
Expected points
A lookup fitted on 2016–2025: each carry by yard line and down, each target by pass depth and yard line, valued in PPR points including fumbles.
Stability
Year-to-year correlation and split-half reliability (odd vs even games). The 2026 estimates pull each number toward his prior by as many carries as the metric needs to be half signal.
Credit model
Ridge regression on designed-run EPA, 2016–2026, penalty chosen by leaving one season out; 80% intervals from game-level resamples. Play-callers come from a hand-checked table where known and the head coach otherwise, so team and play-caller often cannot be separated.
Aging and projections
Age curves follow the same back from one season to the next (survivors only, so the true decline is if anything steeper). Projections use only what was known at the time and were tested one season at a time against naive baselines.
Injuries
An injury episode is one or more games missed in a row. Its type comes from the weekly injury report (2016+), and backs sent straight to injured reserve are pooled separately. Each episode is compared with the back's full games before he got hurt, and with healthy backs over the same weeks.
How it was checked
Four analysis squads each had an independent checker recompute three published numbers by a different route, plus reviewers looking for definition errors, look-ahead and overclaiming. Play-by-play yards and carries match nflverse weekly totals (Barkley 2024: 345 carries, 2,005 yards).
Data: nflverse (NGS, PFR, FTN via nflverse; FTN CC BY-SA 4.0). Companion page: WR breakouts. Built 2026-10-15.
